job_description_info.job_description:
# Full-Stack Engineer (TypeScript / React) – Patient Experience

**Company:** Verdane Care (FICTIONAL)
**Location:** Graz, Austria (hybrid) or fully remote within Austria, Germany, Croatia or Slovenia
**Employment:** Full-time, permanent (or B2B contract in Croatia on request)
**Team:** Patient Experience squad (4 engineers, 1 designer, 1 product manager)

## About the role

Verdane Care makes appointment-booking and follow-up software for private clinics and physiotherapy practices. Patients use our web app and mobile web experience to book visits, fill in intake forms, receive reminders and view exercise plans.

As a Full-Stack Engineer you will build and improve those patient-facing features end to end – from React components and accessibility to the Node.js APIs and the database behind them. You will work in a small squad with a designer and a product manager, and you will ship to production several times a week.

## What you will do

- Build new patient-facing features in React and TypeScript, with a strong focus on accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) and performance on low-end phones
- Implement Node.js (NestJS) APIs and PostgreSQL schemas to support those features
- Integrate with third-party systems such as clinic calendars, SMS providers and payment gateways
- Write unit, integration and end-to-end tests (Jest, Playwright) and keep the build green
- Take part in design reviews, usability sessions and sprint planning
- Handle personal health data responsibly: follow our GDPR and data-minimisation guidelines, support audit requests from clinic customers
- Mentor interns or junior colleagues when the opportunity arises

## What you bring

**Must have**
- 2+ years of professional experience building web applications with React and TypeScript
- Experience writing backend services in Node.js (Express, NestJS or similar) and working with SQL databases
- Understanding of semantic HTML, responsive layouts and web accessibility basics
- Experience with automated testing (unit and end-to-end) and Git-based workflows
- Awareness of web security fundamentals (authentication, OWASP Top 10) and willingness to learn the privacy requirements of health data
- Fluent English; German or Croatian is helpful for customer-facing conversations

**Nice to have**
- Experience with Next.js or other server-side rendering frameworks
- Experience in healthcare, wellness or other regulated environments
- Familiarity with AWS or a similar cloud, and with Docker
- Experience with design systems and Storybook
- Experience with analytics and A/B testing

## What we offer

- Salary range EUR 54,000 – 70,000 gross per year depending on experience (Austrian collective agreement minimum applies)
- 25 days of holiday plus the Austrian public holidays, 5 additional well-being days and a EUR 1,200 yearly education budget
- Flexible hours, a home-office stipend and a yearly team retreat
- A friendly, low-ego team that cares about the people who use our software

## How to apply

Send your CV. A short cover letter and a link to something you have built (a portfolio, a GitHub project or a live site) are welcome but optional. We reply within ten working days.

Verdane Care is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace and welcomes applications from career changers and people returning to work.

Verdane Care is a healthcare technology company founded in Graz in 2019. It develops software that helps private clinics, physiotherapy practices and dental offices manage patient interactions more smoothly. Its products support online appointment booking and reminders, secure digital intake and consent forms, and physiotherapy exercise plans and follow-ups. More than 1,900 practices across Austria, Germany, Croatia and Slovenia use its services.

Verdane’s guiding principles are **“Patients first,” “Privacy by default,” and “Simple beats clever.”** The company emphasizes secure handling of health information, with ISO 27001 certification and hosting in EU data centres, as well as inclusive design: its applications are built to WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility standards and undergo regular audits.

The company has 68 employees based in Graz and Ljubljana, alongside remote colleagues, and is expanding its engineering team. Its engineering practices include weekly demos with clinic staff and optional pair programming, reflecting a focus on user needs and collaboration. Overall, Verdane Care combines practical software development with a mission to make healthcare feel simpler and more human.

## Verdane Care launches redesigned patient app and opens engineering hub in Ljubljana
**Graz, 22 September 2026**

Verdane Care, the Graz-based provider of appointment-booking software for private clinics, has launched a completely redesigned patient experience built on a new React-based design system. The new app cuts the median booking time from 94 to 41 seconds and passes the WCAG 2.2 AA audit commissioned from an independent accessibility consultancy.

The company also opened a small engineering hub in Ljubljana, Croatia, to recruit developers who prefer working in the Adriatic time zone. "Great engineers do not all live in Graz," said co-founder and CTO Jure Kovač. "We are hiring full-stack engineers who care about accessibility and about the people who will use the software."

Co-founder and CEO Dr. Lena Moser announced that Verdane will release a public developer API for clinic software vendors in spring 2027. The company says all patient data remains in EU data centres and that Verdane was recently re-certified under ISO 27001 without findings.

Verdane employs 68 people and plans to hire eight engineers, two designers and one data protection specialist before mid-2027.
# Careers at Verdane Care
*(fictional careers page – verdanecare.example/careers)*

## Join us and make healthcare feel human

**Engineering at Verdane**
- Front end: React, TypeScript, Next.js (marketing and clinic web), Storybook design system, Playwright
- Back end: Node.js (NestJS), PostgreSQL, Redis; AWS (Frankfurt region), Docker, GitHub Actions
- Practices: pair programming on request, weekly demos with real clinic staff, accessibility checks in CI, quarterly security reviews

I am a Computing graduate with First Class Honours and hands-on experience building React and TypeScript applications, accessible interfaces, and a Node.js/Express API using PostgreSQL. Verdane Care’s focus on putting patients first and making healthcare feel simpler and more human strongly appeals to me.

Accessibility has been a consistent focus in my work. During my Software Development Internship at Harbourline Media, I fixed accessibility issues across more than 20 components on its React news site and built a reusable, keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery, documenting it in Storybook. For my final-year project, Tidewatch, I built an accessible React and TypeScript app with a Node.js/Express API and PostgreSQL, and tested it with NVDA and VoiceOver. The project achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.

I have also written unit tests with Jest and React Testing Library, and built a Next.js booking site for a local yoga studio. Together, these projects have given me practical experience building React and TypeScript frontends, a Node.js/Express backend service, and PostgreSQL-backed functionality, while reinforcing the value of thoughtful, user-focused design. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to accessible, user-focused patient experiences with Verdane Care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would be glad to discuss how my experience could contribute to Verdane Care’s Patient Experience team. My portfolio is available at aiyana-bt.example.com.

Yours sincerely,
Aiyana Brooks-Tan

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and well structured. It presents the strongest relevant evidence in a logical order: React/TypeScript and backend foundations, accessibility experience, testing, and the Next.js project. The quantified accessibility result and the reference to more than 20 components provide useful credibility. The motivation is reasonably tailored to Verdane Care's patient-focused mission, although the opening and closing use somewhat similar wording about accessible, user-focused experiences. The letter appropriately avoids claiming that the candidate already has the job's required two-plus years of professional experience or healthcare-data experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter uses ATS-friendly plain text, standard headings are not required for this format, and the main technologies appear in recognizable forms: React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Jest, React Testing Library, Next.js, Storybook, accessibility, NVDA, and VoiceOver. AI screening probability is high for the technologies and accessibility focus that the candidate genuinely supports. The letter does not mention Git-based workflows, despite Git/GitHub being listed in the associated CV, so it misses one supported keyword. It correctly does not add unsupported terms such as NestJS, Playwright, Docker, AWS, OWASP Top 10, GDPR, or health-data privacy experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with React/TypeScript frontend development, Node.js/Express and PostgreSQL project work, accessibility, automated unit testing, Next.js, Storybook, and wellness-related work through the yoga studio booking site. The accessibility examples are particularly relevant to Verdane Care's emphasis on inclusive patient-facing experiences. The candidate does not meet or demonstrate every stated requirement: the material does not establish two-plus years of professional React/TypeScript experience; there is no end-to-end testing evidence; semantic HTML and responsive-layout understanding are not explicitly demonstrated; web-security and OWASP awareness are not documented; health-data privacy experience is not documented; and there is no German or Croatian, AWS, Docker, analytics, or A/B-testing evidence. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects in the letter. The letter also does not explicitly mention Git-based workflows, although that experience is present in the associated CV.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENT:
1. In the third paragraph, after “I have also written unit tests with Jest and React Testing Library,” add a truthful Git-based-workflow reference supported by the associated CV, for example: “I have also used Git and GitHub alongside automated unit testing with Jest and React Testing Library...” Keep the wording limited to unit testing; do not claim integration or end-to-end testing.
2. In the opening paragraph, replace “Verdane Care’s focus on putting patients first and making healthcare feel simpler and more human strongly appeals to me” with a slightly more role-specific sentence that connects the candidate's evidence to the company, for example: “Verdane Care’s focus on making patient-facing healthcare experiences simpler and more human strongly appeals to me, particularly because my projects have focused on accessible, user-focused web experiences.” This reduces generic phrasing while remaining truthful.
3. In the closing paragraph, remove the repetition of “accessible, user-focused” if the revised opening already uses that phrase. For example, change “I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to accessible, user-focused patient experiences with Verdane Care” to “I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to Verdane Care’s Patient Experience team.”
